_doc: One entry per deviation shape. Lifecycle and gating rules: docs/GATING.md. Never delete entries; never flip still_reproduces without a fresh verifying scan. `signal` is a `|`-joined list of canonical names — each token is either a bias-report metric (docs/bias_data.json `metrics`) or a registry signal key (LANGUAGE_DEFINITIONS rules, via tools/_registry.py); no prose, no `+`, no `(various)`; tokens are sorted and unique. The reports join `signal` x `languages_seen` as a cross-product to decide whether a cell is accounted for (docs/GATING.md n/a rule 2 today; red cells from gitgalaxy#2669 E.1), so a token must hold for EVERY language listed — scope a collective entry down rather than let it excuse a cell nobody looked at. An entry that explains no cell (a workflow or classification fact) carries an empty `signal`, which never matches. `languages_seen` may be the sentinel ["all"].

entries.verdict: galaxyscope.py ~2145 ('THE CONTEXTUAL BASELINE FIX'): a file imported by others (popularity > 0) has orphaned_logic converted into api before recording. Micro-repro: 2-def file imported by a sibling records api=4, un-imported records api=2. With the spec's main->a->b->c chain and uncalled probes, api = defs x 2 in a/b/c, defs in main. Deliberate scoring semantics; raw counts unrecoverable from the DB (filed squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2536 asking for raw recording). apex added 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.3): it had no import chain at all until Type.forName('a'/'b'/'c') was planted, so a/b/c had popularity 0 and api 0; with the chain live their 3 uncalled probes convert to api 3 each, exactly this shape. GATE KEY CHANGE (gitgalaxy#2729, 2026-09-04): the conversion no longer reaches the manifest's `api` -- verify_language.py reads raw_arch_api there -- and is pinned instead as `api_orphan_credit` = arch_api - raw_arch_api, which this entry now covers. Semantics unchanged: credit = the file's uncalled probe count in a/b/c (3), 0 in main (popularity 0). Still the gate's only assertion that the main->a->b->c import chain resolved.

Keywords inside one string literal ('if eval fails, try open') count toward branch (+2), safety (+1), io (+1) but eval does NOT count toward high_risk_execution (routes to sec_tainted_injection instead). Micro-repro: identical files differing only in literal content, scanned end-to-end. Comments are fully stripped (verified 0 contribution); strings are inconsistently half-counted. 2026-08-31 cross-language extension: javascript reproduces python exactly (same decoy sentence, if/try count, eval does not); cobol does NOT shield at all (ALTER counts high_risk_execution from inside a DISPLAY literal) — the shielding is lexical-family-dependent, i.e. itself a language bias. 2026-08-31 legacy batch: fortran/ada/assembly count literals like cobol (fortran IF+GOTO+OPEN all count; ada 'if' counts; asm jmp/syscall count, and ARM's single-letter 'b' mnemonic even matches the filename inside %include "b.asm"); abap is a THIRD profile — shields branch/high_risk/io but NOT safety (TRY in a literal counts safety, isolated by micro-repro with comment-only vs string-only files). Worst amplification: a branch keyword inside a literal creates phantom branch context that triples state_mutation via the flux weighting (see state-flux-branch-weighting). Current behavior baked into manifests; whether intentional is the upstream question. 2026-08-31 batch 3 (12 mainstream languages): the selective profile (high-risk family shielded, branch/safety/io count) holds for c/cpp/csharp/java/go/kotlin/typescript/php/lua/swift; ruby counts eval from the literal (eval-as-bypass, like shell); perl's eval survives only because its bypass rule requires eval-followed-by-quote/paren (syntax shielding, not surface shielding); swift's api rule counts the word 'open' inside the literal (API-exposure mass from prose). try counts branch in csharp/java/kotlin/php/perl/swift/typescript. Swift's bare-open api FP filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2544. 2026-08-31 batch 4 (Tier-1 completion): a FOURTH profile — scheme's sexp-anchored branch keywords shield strings by SYNTAX (bare 'if' in a literal cannot match the paren-anchored rule) while its unanchored eval still counts; m4 is fully inert by the same mechanism (macro-name keywords). matlab and tcl join shell/ruby in counting eval-as-bypass from literals. dockerfile/makefile/livecode count literals wholesale. swift-open-style api hit not repeated elsewhere. RESOLVED-AS-EXPLAINED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy#2535 closed as not-a-bug after root-cause isolation. There is NO string-literal shielding mechanism anywhere in the engine -- strings are never stripped/masked from the code stream for any structural signal, in any language (only comments are). Every observed 'shielding' shape here is the ordinary Silencer Region dampener (spatial_correlation.py apply_dampener_correlations Block 2: high_risk_execution <- safety, 500-char radius) firing because the shared decoy sentence 'if eval fails, try open' happens to contain both a real danger keyword AND a real safety keyword for SOME languages, by accident of English-word/rule-vocabulary overlap -- not a deliberate per-language shielding design. Isolated via direct micro-repro: python state_danger 0->1 the instant 'try' is swapped out of the decoy with nothing else changed. Per-language explanation for the profiles recorded above: python/js/haskell/abap ('shielded'/'inverted') all have TRY (or their language's equivalent) in their OWN safety rule, so the dampener fires; cobol/fortran/ada/assembly ('unshielded') do NOT have TRY in their safety rule (cobol's is END-IF/END-PERFORM/.../VALIDATE/CHECK), so it never fires; rust's 'shielded' reading was actually a THIRD, unrelated cause -- its high_risk_execution rule has no 'eval' concept at all (panic!/todo!/process::exit), a morphology mismatch, not shielding. The #2546 'phantom branch trigger from string literals' shares this exact explanation (no shielding exists, so a genuinely-present branch keyword correctly triggers the flux dampener regardless of surface). Follow-up filed as a CORPUS issue (decoy sentence design), not an engine issue -- see keyword-rosetta issue tracking decoy redesign. capstones jcl.md/cobol.md/python.md corrected to match. DECOY REDESIGN PILOT 2026-09-01 (keyword-rosetta#17): python/fortran/rust re-authored to a danger-only literal ('plain eval|ASSIGN|abort decoy text') per the redesigned SPEC §String decoy. All three profiles converge on the same clean read -- the danger keyword counts +1 from inside the literal, undampened: python eval +1 (was 0 under the old sentence's try-collision), fortran ASSIGN +1 (GOTO retired from the decoy: it doubles as a branch keyword and fed the x3 flux -- state_mutation 6->2), rust abort +1 (the first time rust's decoy tested anything; eval matches nothing in its danger rule; state 6->2). One new engine fact surfaced by the pilot and now recorded in SPEC: dampener correlations are function-scoped, but MODULE-LEVEL code falls back to flat 500-char-radius behavior (apply_dampener_correlations docstring) -- python's literal initially read 0 at module level because probe_safety's assert sat ~450 chars away; moving it inside probe_globals isolated it. DECOY REDESIGN COMPLETE 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.1 wave 2, 32 languages; A.3 wave 3, abap/assembly/cobol/sqlite): all 40 languages_seen now carry a danger-only literal, gates green. Screening rule that made it mechanical: run the candidate literal through the language's live compiled rules and require exactly one high_risk_execution hit and zero hits in any SCORED column -- the planted set plus the seven non-planted signals that feed a risk_* formula (_registry.risk_dependencies(): concurrency, sync_locks, reflection_metaprogramming, immutability_locks, spec_exposure, debug_prints, llm_api). That rejected Thread.Abort (csharp), Thread.stop (java) and iex (powershell), each clean against the planted set alone. Filler words need the same check: 'text' matches dart's and embedded_python's ui_framework rule. Findings from the sweep: matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval under safety_bypasses, NOT high_risk_execution, so their old decoy exercised the wrong family (safety_bypasses 3->2 each); swift's api rule counted the prose 'open' (api 4->3, a scored planted column fed from inside a string, the #2544 shape); abap's recorded 'third profile' was the Silencer Region after all -- dropping TRY takes its TRUNCATE 0->1; scheme moved no count at all, its sexp-anchored branch rule never having matched the prose 'if'; assembly keeps its x3 flux because probe_state's own 'ret' is a branch keyword, unlike the 35 languages where the retired 'if' was the only branch in scope. sqlite needs a two-word literal ('DROP DATABASE') -- its danger vocabulary has no single bare token. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the field now names every column this shape moves, not just the headline four — state_mutation (the x3 flux amplification), safety_bypasses (matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval there, not under high_risk_execution) and api (swift's rule counting the prose 'open', #2544) are consequences recorded in the verdict above and are joined on here. DECOY COVERAGE AUDIT 2026-09-06 (keyword-rosetta#71): the "all 40 languages_seen now carry a danger-only literal" claim above was one language wrong in each direction. agc_assembly was listed but has NEVER carried one and cannot (no character-literal type in the AGC assembler -- see string-decoy-unplantable-no-literal-surface, which now owns its high_risk_execution cell); yacc has carried one in b.y since the redesign but its manifest decoys array was empty, so it was never listed here. agc_assembly is REMOVED from languages_seen: its -33% high_risk_execution cell was reading as `ledgered` off a premise that was false for it, which is exactly the excuse-a-cell-nobody-looked-at failure this file's _doc warns about. yacc is deliberately NOT added -- its high_risk_execution sits at the median, so it needs no excuse, and adding it would cross-product this entry's other six signals onto yacc cells nobody screened for this shape. The four remaining gaps the audit found (css, html, jcl, yaml -- every language reading high_risk_execution 2 against a median 3, and the exact set with no string decoy) are now planted rather than ledgered, each by WIDENING an existing construct so no second signal moves: jcl PARM='PLAIN PGM=IKJEFT01 DECOY' on the existing PROBESTATE step (a new EXEC step would have cost func_start+1 and args+1, which is why #71 opened as a question); yaml NOTE: "plain eval decoy text" as the value of probe_state's existing env key; css content: "plain expression decoy text" inside the existing @keyframes probe-state block; html the text node of the existing <div id="probe-api-b">, since html's literal surface is markup TEXT (an attribute value would have moved args). All four measured +1 high_risk_execution and nothing else, end-to-end. 2026-09-06 (gitgalaxy#2815): the 'worst amplification' clause above -- a branch keyword inside a literal tripling real nearby mutations -- can no longer reach a recorded count: the x3 is applied only in the score layer's weighted view, so a phantom branch context moves risk_state_flux / cognitive load but never state_mutation as a manifest reads it. The literal-shielding facts this entry records (which rules count a keyword inside a string) are unchanged and still_reproduces stays true. SIGNAL NARROWED 2026-09-06 (Phase 0 cause triage, gitgalaxy docs/contract_roadmap.md): was `api|branch|high_risk_execution|io|safety|safety_bypasses|state_mutation`, now `high_risk_execution|safety_bypasses` -- the only columns a danger-only literal can move (the +1 high_risk_execution the SPEC expects, and safety_bypasses where matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval there). Since the decoy redesign no corpus literal carries a branch, io, safety, api or state_mutation keyword, so this entry's cross-product was excusing 22 cells it could not explain: 12 branch, 5 io, 3 safety, 2 safety_bypasses. Re-read one by one from the manifest notes: ada/fortran/shell/livecode/makefile/powershell/tcl branch, c/javascript/lua/sqlite/tcl io, embedded_python/haskell safety and fortran/haskell safety_bypasses were already carried by their own entries; cpp/csharp/ruby/sqlite/swift branch (catch, goto, rescue, CASE..END, guard-else) and typescript safety (unknown/never) had NO other entry -- filed as gitgalaxy#2822 and ledgered as branch-counts-non-decision-keywords / typescript-type-keywords-count-as-safety. Disposition stays engine-semantic: strings count, deliberately, and the corpus plants around it.

entries.verdict: python's test rule includes \bassert\b and the safety rule includes assert: one planted assert counts both. Legitimate overlapping taxonomies; record +1 test wherever a safety assert is planted. Also c (bare assert( in both rules) and perl (ok( in the test rule alongside croak/confess safety plants). RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (assert removed from the test rule, still matched by safety): a.py test dropped 3->2. Still reproduces for c/perl (their own rule files are unchanged). RESOLVED for c and perl 2026-09-07 by gitgalaxy#2852 (test contract): c's bare assert( left the test rule (contract C1 -- the runtime guard is safety's, the #2626 python resolution stated as a rule); a.c test 3->2. perl's mechanism was measured to be different from this entry's framing: croak/confess never matched the test rule -- the +1 was Test::More::ok($kit) firing twice (module name + ok( call form), settled by contract C2 (a module qualifier is not a separate hit from the call it qualifies, (?!::) guard); a.pl test 3->2. The entry closes; the python assert overlap remains the deliberate safety-side surface (assert still matched by safety in all three languages, mass conserved). 2026-09-08: gitgalaxy#2869 restates the boundary from safety's side (corollary C3: the language's runtime guard is safety's hit, never test's); no counts move.

python-family io rule matches the os./sys. prefixes that the globals plants (os.environ, sys.argv) necessarily carry: +2 io in whichever file hosts probe_globals. RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (io rule gained negative lookaheads excluding os.environ/sys.argv from the io match): a.py io dropped 3->1. No other language currently in languages_seen.

Debt rules are whole-text, not comment-anchored, and '-' is a regex word boundary: HACK-LEVEL (data item, 2 code occurrences) counts fragile_debt, PROBE-TODO (paragraph name) counts planned_debt. Python's HACK_LEVEL is inert only because '_' is a word character — tokenization luck, not surface anchoring. Real-world FP shapes: COBOL BUG-COUNT/WS-FIX-FLAG, css .bug-icon, lisp fix-me. Filed upstream; observed counts baked into cobol manifest until fixed. Batch 4: scheme reproduces it — (define (probe-todo ...)) records planned_debt 2 (comment + identifier), confirming the lisp-family exposure predicted in #2537. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2622 (closes #2537) — hyphenated-identifier guards ((?<![A-Za-z0-9]-) / (?!-[A-Za-z0-9])) on the shared GLOBAL_FRAGILE_DEBT/GLOBAL_PLANNED_DEBT patterns. Fresh verifying scan (engine at PR #2622 head): cobol c.cpy fragile_debt 3->1, planned_debt 2->1; scheme c.scm planned_debt 2->1 — only the planted * HACK: / * TODO: / ;; TODO: comments count. Real comment markers incl. the hyphen-adjacent family (-- TODO, --TODO, TODO--) verified still counting via the upstream PR's strict tests. Manifests re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4.

A bare token + period in Area B (CEE3DMP. / CEEMOUT., column 12) is counted as a paragraph header: func_start regex's post-sequence-area [ \t]* tolerates any indentation (relaxed/free-format support). By strict reference format a paragraph-name must start in Area A. b.cpy records func_start 5 (3 real paragraphs + 2). Whether the relaxed tolerance is deliberate is the upstream question. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2552 (closes #2538 -- func_start no longer mistakes LE service calls for paragraphs). Fresh verifying scan (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2552/#2611): b.cpy func_start 5->3, api 5->3 (orphan conversion follows), telemetry/safety_bypasses/state_mutation unchanged at 2/2/2 -- only the two bare-token FPs vanished. Manifest re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4. Surfaced by the first all-language CI run since #2552 merged (rosetta PR #5, which touches no data/ so the gate ran all 46).

'with (shape) {}' is parsed as a function named 'with' by the identifier(args){ alternation: the keyword exclusion list has if/for/while/switch/catch/return but not with. finditer-confirmed; switch (flag) {} in the same corpus is correctly excluded. b.js records func_start/args 4 for 3 functions. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2539 ('with' added to the func_start/args statement-keyword exclusions, JS and TS): b.js func_start/args/api 4->3.

cobol globals pattern includes WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION as an alternative — every fixed-format program with a working-storage section records globals >= 1. keyword_menu.py missed it (multi-word alternation; the miner only validates single-token candidates) — menu-tool improvement noted. main.cbl globals 1 baked in. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy #2805 (gitgalaxy#2830): the globals rule dropped WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION (a region header, not shared state); GLOBAL/EXTERNAL/COMMON remain. Verifying scan on engine main ffa0a0f: main.cbl globals 1->0, a.cpy still 2 (the planted items), cobol aggregate 3->2 = median. main.cbl globals re-blessed to 0 in this PR.

Token signals match ordinary identifiers that happen to spell a keyword: js probeIo's parameter named 'path' counts io +1 (path is a js io keyword). Inherent to keyword-based signals. Authoring guidance: avoid naming identifiers after menu keywords unless the collision is the point; record it when unavoidable. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): narrowed from the prose '(any token signal)' to `io`, the one collision actually verified (javascript probeIo's `path` parameter). The shape generalises but the ledger must not claim to explain a cell nobody has looked at; a new collision is a new occurrence, added when observed. RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by gitgalaxy#2841 (io contract C1): bare `path` left javascript's io rule -- an everyday word fires only in its operative form (require('path') / path.join), so the one verified collision (probeIo's `path` parameter) cannot fire. main.js io 4->3. Verified by rule_probe io before/after and rosetta_audit 46/46 against fix/2841-io-contract. C1 is the standing authoring guidance.

state_mutation is recorded x3 when branch context exists in the file ('flux' semantics, matching the state_flux column name). Micro-repro: one := inside a real ada if -> 3; one := with no branch -> 1; the multiplier applies file-wide to all mutations. python/cobol corpus files were exact only because their b files had no branch context. Consequence of #2535: a branch keyword inside a string literal creates PHANTOM branch context and triples unrelated real mutations ('while' in a string: 2 raw := -> 6). REFINED (batch 3, go micro-evidence): the x3 weighting is PER-FUNCTION, not per-file — go b.go records 11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 (its own string carries the branch keyword) + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1 (no branch context in that function). Reproduces in all 12 batch-3 languages whose state rules have raw hits alongside the string decoy. Batch 4 adds the three cleanest per-function proofs: matlab main = 12 = one function's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1; powershell c stays x1 because probe_debt has no return/branch while its sibling does; dockerfile scopes flux per RUN instruction (4 = 1x3 + 1x1). DOCUMENTED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy PR #2631 (closes #2546) resolves the upstream question as deliberate design, kept and now documented + test-pinned. SEMANTICS CORRECTION to this entry's earlier description: the x3 is a 150-CHARACTER proximity radius per mutation within the same function (spatial_correlation.py Block 6, correlate_scoped) -- NOT a blanket per-function branch-context toggle; corpus probe functions were simply shorter than the radius, which masked the distinction (the per-function refinement was correct about scoping, wrong about the trigger being function-wide). Raw counts are recoverable as recorded - 2*amplified_cascading_flux (per-file mitigation_telemetry, audit report 'Contextual Mitigations & Amplifications'). Behavior unchanged, so still_reproduces stays true; the actionable blocker for the corpus's state_mutation median inflation is now #2535 ALONE (the phantom literal trigger) -- language tracking issues' state_mutation residuals re-point there. 2026-09-01 (gitgalaxy#2634 / #2545 landing): this entry's powershell `c` evidence line no longer discriminates — with `return` out of `branch`, probe_todo has no branch context either, so powershell c is x1 throughout and c branch is 0. The go / matlab / dockerfile per-function proofs are untouched and remain this entry's evidence. Same landing removes the phantom `return` context that was tripling apex c.cls (state_mutation 3 -> 1, re-baselined with it): a real reduction in flux inflation, not a semantics change. 2026-09-03 (gitgalaxy#2654 / engine PR gitgalaxy#2703): the matlab per-function proof is RETIRED and matlab drops out of languages_seen. matlab main.m's `12 = probe_branch's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1` only ever existed because every one of those raw hits was the `out = <value>` return convention counted as a mutation -- probe_branch's three `out = k` are three `return k`, which every other language records as zero. With the engine's `matlab_return_channel` scope filter the file records 0, and no matlab probe function now has a mutation alongside branch context, so the language exhibits no flux amplification at all. It was NOT re-planted: a matlab-only mutation added to keep the demonstration would break the 12-probe program's cross-language equivalence, which is what makes this corpus able to find shapes like #2654 in the first place. go's b.go (11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1) and dockerfile's per-RUN scoping (4 = 1x3 + 1x1) are unaffected and remain this entry's per-function evidence. 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2764 / engine PR gitgalaxy#2779): assembly drops out of languages_seen. b.asm's `state_mutation` 6 = probe_state's raw 2 (inc + dec) x3, and the branch context inside that 150-character radius was the function's own `ret`. With call/ret/jmp out of `branch`, b.asm has no branch context anywhere and the file records its raw 2 -- the same real reduction in flux inflation #2634 produced for apex c.cls, not a semantics change. assembly was the only language in the corpus where the amplifier fired on a keyword that was not a decision; go's b.go and dockerfile's per-RUN scoping remain this entry's per-function evidence. RESOLVED 2026-09-06 (gitgalaxy#2815, contract roadmap Phase 2 / decision D1): the recorded state_mutation is now the raw hit count for every file. The x3 weighting keeps its semantics (same 150-char same-function radius, same amplified_cascading_flux tally) but is applied only in the score layer's weighted view (core/spatial_correlation.py PROXIMITY_WEIGHTS / weighted_count()), never in the count a manifest reads. Verifying scan: the full 46-language sweep against gitgalaxy fix/2813-raw-counts (8284c71e) passed every state_mutation assertion unchanged -- this entry's languages_seen list had already decayed (since gitgalaxy#2634 and #2779 removed return/ret/call from branch, no corpus probe carries a branch within 150 chars of a mutation), which is why Phase 0's decayed-entry check listed it. The go / matlab / dockerfile per-function proofs remain a correct description of the weighted view; risk_state_flux is unchanged by construction.

'USE A' does not resolve to a.f90 in the dependency DAG (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires); 'USE a' resolves. Fortran is case-insensitive, the suffix-map lookup is not. Corpus lowercased its USE targets to keep the DAG probe live; real uppercase legacy fortran (very common) silently loses its dependency graph. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2540 (per-language case-folded fallback in the DAG suffix-map lookup for fortran/cobol/haskell, scoped to the importing language's own files): uppercase 'USE A' now resolves; corpus values unchanged (targets were lowercased as the workaround). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api` — the two the verdict actually pins (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires). The corpus never showed the wider graph family deviating because the USE targets were lowercased as the workaround.

ada's closing 'end if' re-matches \bif\b: every well-formed if statement counts branch at least twice (if + end if). Same class would apply to fortran 'END IF' spelled with a space (corpus used ENDIF, which is inert). Inherent to token-based branch counting on block-closed languages; baked in (main.adb branch 4). RESOLVED 2026-09-06 by gitgalaxy#2822 (branch contract, corollary 2): the closing 'end if'/'end case'/'end loop' re-matches are guarded with lookbehinds; main.adb branch 4->3, re-blessed to plant.

GOTO is in both fortran's branch rule and its high_risk_execution rule — one planted GOTO counts both. finditer-confirmed. RESOLVED 2026-09-06 by gitgalaxy#2822 (corollary 3): GOTO left branch; high_risk_execution alone owns it. main.f90 branch 4->3. 2026-09-08 gitgalaxy#2878 (high_risk_execution contract C3): GOTO left high_risk_execution as well -- a jump inside the unit is nobody's signal (as in c/go/perl/php); main.f90's `GOTO 100` re-planted as `STOP`. Both halves of the old dual are now stated; entry stays retired.

assembly's branch rule includes call and ret (all control transfers) — correct for asm morphology but it means every probe body's ret and every glue call counts branch (main.asm: 10 = 3 call + 4 ret + 3 planted jumps). Cross-language branch comparisons must expect asm to run structurally hot. RESOLVED 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2764, engine PR gitgalaxy#2779): filed and fixed. `branch` feeds only decision-DENSITY metrics (avg_func_complexity, max_func_complexity, func_internal_density, cog_raw, control_flow_ratio, risk_cognitive_load) plus #2546's x3 flux amplifier, so counting call/ret/jmp made cognitive load track subroutine COUNT -- what functions_found already measures -- and assembly was the only corpus language where the flux amplifier fired at all (its branch context was a `ret`). #2545's precedent applies verbatim: `ret` IS `return`, and no other language's branch rule counts its call syntax. jmp|call|ret|b|bl|bx|blr were RELOCATED to structural_boundaries (not deleted), so branch+linear mass per file is conserved and control_flow_ratio's denominator is unchanged. Corpus effect: branch 25 -> 3 hits (main 10->3, a 4->0, b 5->0, c 5->0), and probe_branch's own `jmp` plant was re-authored to `jz` so all three planted hits are real conditionals. Verified by a fresh galaxyscope --db-only run over data/assembly on the #2779 build (PASS, 76 assertions). Sibling shape in agc_assembly fixed in the same PR (TC|TCF|TCR|CALL|GOTO|RESUME|RETURN out of branch, CCS de-duplicated out of structural_boundaries).

ARM's single-letter 'b' branch mnemonic matches the word b anywhere literals count — including the filename inside %include "b.asm" (a.asm branch +1, finditer-confirmed). Any asm file mentioning a bare 'b' in a string/path gains branch mass. Sub-case of #2535's literal counting; not filed separately. AMENDED 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2764): the collision itself still reproduces -- a bare `b` in a string or path is still matched -- but `b` moved from `branch` to `structural_boundaries` with the rest of the unconditional-transfer family, so it no longer inflates a DECISION count. a.asm branch 4 -> 0. structural_boundaries is not a SPEC-planted signal and no manifest asserts it, so the shape now explains no gated cell; the `signal` token was repointed rather than the entry retired, because the underlying literal-counting cause (#2535) is unchanged.

Top-level value bindings (CAFs like 'region = unsafePerformIO ...') count func_start/args like any function binding — morphologically correct for haskell, where top-level values ARE nullary functions. a.hs records 5 (3 probes + 2 planted globals). Type-signature + binding pairs count once, not twice (verified).

finally is in both haskell's cleanup and safety rules (finditer-confirmed on c.hs) — one planted finally counts both. RESOLVED 2026-09-08 by gitgalaxy#2869 (safety contract, corollary C3 one-owner): `finally` is the release combinator and cleanup's alone -- it left haskell's safety rule; c.hs safety 1->0, cleanup unchanged at 2.

shell's branch rule counts the test brackets [ and ] as branch tokens (finditer on main.sh: if,[,],then,fi = 5 for one conditional) — every bracketed test costs +2 branch on top of if/then/fi. Defensible ([ is the test builtin) but a strong per-language inflation for cross-language branch comparisons. RESOLVED 2026-09-06 by gitgalaxy#2822 (corollary 2): the test brackets and then/fi/esac/done left branch for structural_boundaries; probe_branch re-planted with an else arm and a while loop, main.sh branch 5->3.

'trap : TERM' counts globals: the TERM signal name collides with the TERM env-var keyword in shell's globals rule (a.sh globals 3 for 2 planted). Any trap handler naming TERM/USER-adjacent signals inherits this. RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by gitgalaxy#2858 (globals contract corollary 3, the ambiguity anchor): shell's rule counts an environment variable only in its variable form -- `$NAME` / `${NAME` or a top-level `NAME=` / `export NAME=` -- so a bare signal name, a log string or a comment word no longer fires (crucible 174->141: the removed hits were `trap ... INT TERM`, `"etcd must be in your PATH"`, `# HOME verification`). Verifying scan against fix/2858-globals-contract: a.sh globals 3->2 = median; re-blessed here.

Recorded as observed; gitgalaxy#2536 (raw hit_vector recording) would make these auditable. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2618 (closes #2547 -- synthetic slicer bucket names excluded from the orphan/duplicate census). Fresh verifying scans (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2618): the inflating orphans were the synthetic buckets themselves -- __global_context__ in livecode/lua/matlab/ruby/shell a- AND b-files (api -1 each; lua a 9->8, b 10->9), and sqlite b.sql/c.sql whose 'functions' are ALL synthetic names (CREATE_Statement/SELECT_Statement/UPDATE_Statement/Declarative_Block), so every conversion there vanishes (a.sql 2->0, b.sql 4->0, c.sql 3->0). Real probe functions unaffected everywhere; 13 manifest cells re-baselined in this change per GATING step 4. lua/ruby added to languages_seen (same __global_context__ shape, confirmed). dockerfile/powershell manifests needed no change (their counts never included the bucket). First live catch of the #2557 rosetta-audit system (run locally against pull/2618/head pre-merge).

^.read counts BOTH import and io (finditer-confirmed) — every corpus chain link adds +1 io in sqlite. By design (a .read is file io), but a cross-language io comparison must expect it. RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by gitgalaxy#2841 (io contract C2): .read/.import are import's hits alone; sqlite io counts what leaves the engine (readfile/writefile, .output/.dump family). Every corpus chain link stops adding io +1; main.sql io 5->3 with the probe_io re-plant, a.sql 1->0, b.sql 3->0.

GalaxyScope's census enumerates git-tracked files only; an untracked folder scans as '0 files mapped' with no per-file warning. Authoring workflow requires commit-before-verify (SPEC.md). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `signal` is deliberately EMPTY. This is a workflow fact, not an explanation for any cell — an untracked folder produces no numbers at all — and an empty signal never matches the metric x language join, so it can never excuse a deviation.

The <?php open tag's ? matches php's branch rule bare ternary-? alternation (finditer-confirmed): EVERY php file records branch >= 1 from its own open tag. A systematic per-file +1 on all real-world PHP; worth an upstream look at excluding ?> / <? tag context from the ? alternation. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2541 (tag context excluded from the ternary-? alternation via (?<!<)?(?!>) guards): per-file tag +1 gone, corpus php branch main 4->3, a/c 1->0, b 3->2.

kotlin's branch rule counts return: every file's branch = returns + real branch keywords (main.kt 8 = 5 returns + if/else/when; files with only returns record branch 3). Same cross-language-inflation class as assembly's call/ret. Batch 4: apex, objective-c, powershell, and zig (pattern-confirmed) also count return — it is a 5-language family, not a kotlin quirk; scala/dart/groovy siblings do not. Strengthens #2545's inconsistency framing. Batch 5: solidity is the 6th member (main branch 8 = 5 returns + 3 keywords). RESOLVED 2026-09-01: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2545 (PR #2634). Checked 11 close siblings across every relevant family (java/c/rust/go/csharp/scala/dart/groovy/swift/typescript/cpp) -- none count bare return as branch, including rust/csharp which share kotlin/zig's exact early-return idiom; no defensible rationale found for any of the 6. Fix split by whether return was already tracked elsewhere: kotlin/apex/powershell/zig had it duplicated under structural_boundaries already (pure de-dup); objective-c/solidity had no other rule tracking it, so return moved there instead of being deleted (signal preserved, same convention). Re-verified against engine pull/2634/head: all 6 gates PASS, branch now matches planted intent EXACTLY in every file (main 3, b 2, a/c 0) across all 6 languages. Real downstream ripple confirmed and re-baselined: apex c.cls state_mutation 3->1 (the manifest's own pre-fix note had already predicted this -- c's return was providing phantom branch context that #2546's x3 flux weighting amplified; removing return-as-branch removed the phantom trigger, leaving the raw hit).

kotlin's object declaration is the globals plant AND counts class_start (a.kt class_start 2) — a documented tier-1 exception to the no-classes tripwire, like cobol's PROGRAM-ID: object IS kotlin's singleton-class construct. RE-DISPOSITIONED 2026-09-07 (gitgalaxy#2856 class_start contract C3): keyword-overlap -> intended-morphology. `object` IS kotlin's singleton-class declaration (class_start) AND is how the globals plant must be written -- Kotlin has no module-level mutable state -- so class_start 2 is plant-forced morphology (#2796's reading), a deliberate dual, not an extraction defect.

swift's _dependency_capture requires module names of 2+ characters ([a-zA-Z_][\w.]+), so 'import a' captures nothing: the corpus's swift chain never resolves, popularity stays 0, and no orphan->api conversion fires. Real single-letter modules are rare but the +-quantifier looks unintentional next to other languages' * shapes. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2543 (capture tail [\w.]+ -> [\w.]*): 'import a' captures, the swift chain resolves, orphan->api conversion fires (a/c api 0->3, b 1->4). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api`, the two the verdict pins.

go's safety_bypasses rule's dot-import alternation (\bimport\s+(?:\.[ \t]+)?") matches EVERY quoted import, not just dot-imports: +1 bypasses per importing file corpus-wide. The (?:\.[ \t]+)? being optional makes the dot-import detector fire on all imports. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2542 (dot made mandatory in the alternation): plain quoted imports no longer count, corpus go safety_bypasses main/a 1->0, b 3->2.

Languages whose visibility IS a naming/declaration convention count it wholesale: go's encapsulation rule counts every lowercase top-level symbol (7-9 per corpus file), perl's counts every my declaration (3-4 per file). Correct morphology, but cross-language encapsulation comparisons must expect these to run structurally hot.

typescript's args rule counts statement-position call parens (describe(kit), expect(kit)) in addition to declaration params — a.ts args 5 for 3 declarations (finditer-confirmed). Plants that are bare calls contaminate args in ts. Batch 4: apex and groovy count statement-position calls the same way (main args 7 = 4 sigs + 3 dispatch calls); objective-c over-counts via selector-colon segments (related morphology, recorded per-manifest). FIXED 2026-09-06 for the two languages this entry is named for, by squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2773 (PR #2786, engine 0b2e9b20), which gave `args` a stated contract (docs/args_rule_contract.md: "args matches the parameters a callable declares") and anchored both rules to it. typescript: the class-member arm was `^[ \t]*IDENT(...)` with no declaration anchor at all, and now requires the parameter list to be followed by a body `{` or a `:` return type; a.ts args 5 -> 3. objective-c: the selector arm matched every keyword-message SEND (a send is lexically identical to the untyped `label:name` parameter shape) and the plain-C arm accepted any `name(...)` followed by `{`/`;`, so free/abort/XCTAssert all scored; both are now anchored, main 6 -> 4 and a/b/c 5 -> 3. Both languages land on the planted 13 exactly, which is the mechanical check that the anchors are correct and not merely narrower. The apex and groovy arm of the original verdict is NOT fixed and moves to args-call-site-counting-apex-groovy, which carries their own upstream issues.

Split out of ts-callparen-args on 2026-09-06 when squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2773 fixed that entry's typescript and objective-c arms but not these two. apex and groovy still count statement-position CALLS as declared parameters: apex main args 7 = 4 signatures + probeBranch/probeIo/probeRisk dispatch calls, a.cls 5 = 3 + isAccessible/StripInaccessible (both `safety` plants); groovy main 7 the same way, c.groovy 5 = 3 + close/dispose (both `cleanup` plants), a.groovy 4 = 3 + assertEquals (a `test` plant). Corpus-wide apex reads 18 and groovy 19 against a planted 13. Cause in both is the same shape #2773 fixed elsewhere: a `^[ \t]*IDENT(...)` member arm whose return-type prefix can match zero times (apex: the return type carries a trailing `?`; groovy: the run is `{0,3}`, and `def` means a method genuinely can have no return type), so the alternative degenerates to the shape of a bare call statement. java and csharp -- the same rule family -- make the return type mandatory; javascript anchors on a `(?=[ \t\n]*\{)` body lookahead. Baked in per the ledger's upstream-bug rule: the corpus measures what the engine does, not what it should. Re-bless both manifests to 13 when the engine fix lands. FIXED 2026-09-06 by squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2783 (apex) and #2782 (groovy), both merged in PR #2790 (engine 2ca956ac), which anchored each member arm to a real declaration the way gitgalaxy#2773 did for typescript and objective-c. apex main.cls 7 -> 4 / a.cls 5 -> 3; groovy main 7 -> 4, a 4 -> 3, c 5 -> 3. Both languages land on the planted 13 exactly -- the same mechanical check ts-callparen-args used, and the reason this is a fix rather than a merely narrower rule. Re-blessed here against engine main; verify_language.py reports 0 mismatches for both and no other cell moved.

m4 and scheme have _dependency_capture = None: include()/(import ...) count the import signal but can never produce a DAG edge, so popularity stays 0 and orphans never convert, corpus-wide. Two whole languages invisible to network_risk_sensor by construction — worth an upstream note whether deliberate. Batch 5: yacc (#include counted, capture None) and markdown (no import rule at all) join — four registry languages structurally invisible to the DAG. scheme RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2652 (added _dependency_capture handling both the corpus's bare (import a) form and real R7RS/Guile library-list forms) -- removed from languages_seen; m4/markdown/yacc remain. SCOPE CORRECTION (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): markdown REMOVED from languages_seen — the entry had it as "no import rule at all", but a None `import` rule is not a None `_dependency_capture`. markdown defines a live capture (the inline-link form `[text](target)`) and its DAG resolves: dependency_links 3, popularity 0.75, betweenness 0.0833, producer_ratio 0.5, i.e. the same values as python/fortran/swift. Its `import` cell is n/a (no rule), which is markdown-lit-plane-morphology's business, not this entry's. m4 and yacc remain, and the scan confirms the full pinned profile they share: dependency_links 0, dependency_density 0, popularity 0, betweenness 0, closeness 0, producer_ratio 0, pagerank at the uniform 1/N 0.2, normalized_blast_radius 200, api 0 (orphans never convert) and therefore risk_api_exposure 0.0 against a 5.29 median — that last one is the red cell this entry has to own, so the signal list names it. Batch C's C.3 removes m4/yacc once #2652's capture shape is extended to them. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2685, Batch C.2 of gitgalaxy#2669, 2026-09-02): m4 and yacc both gained a _dependency_capture built on #2652's shape -- m4 for all four include spellings past m4 quoting, yacc for the prologue #include its `import` signal already counted -- so languages_seen is now empty and still_reproduces is false. Verified by a fresh scan on the engine PR, not by hand: the pinned profile this entry described is gone for both languages, replaced by exactly the healthy sibling profile (popularity 1/1/1/0, producer_ratio 0.5/0.5/1.0/0, non-uniform pagerank, dependency_density 1.0 on a/b and 0.1667-0.2 on main), and the red cell the entry owned -- risk_api_exposure 0.0 against a 5.29 median -- closes because api now converts (0 -> 3 on a/b/c, reblessed in this PR's manifests). The remaining orphan of this shape is neither m4 nor yacc: see gitgalaxy#2684, where the popularity tally credits every same-stemmed file in a scan, which is a different defect in the same subsystem. FIGURES SUPERSEDED (gitgalaxy#2789, 2026-09-06): the dependency_density values quoted above for the resolved m4/yacc profile ("1.0 on a/b and 0.1667-0.2 on main") were measured under the old definition, import_count / max(int(coding_loc * control_flow_ratio), 1), whose denominator collapsed to 1 on any branchless file -- so "1.0 on a/b" was the raw import count, not a density. Under the current definition, import_count / max(coding_loc, EVIDENCE_MASS_FLOOR), the same healthy profile now reads 0.02 on a/b and 0.02 on main. Re-checked at the new values: the profile is still the healthy sibling shape and the entry's resolution is unaffected -- m4 and yacc remain resolved, still_reproduces stays false. Only the quoted numbers are stale, and they are kept above rather than rewritten because they are what was measured at the time.

Also two rule-level divergences on byte-similar code: embedded io drops os./sys. (python counts them), and orphan->api conversion does not fire under embedded classification. The micro-repro still records the JS body's own signals, so the payload handshake is intact. Manifests re-blessed in this PR; from here the cell's live cause is html-func-start-counts-script-elements.

AGC's real 1960s YUL/GAP instruction set (agc_assembly.py:99-101, comment: 'AGC lacks native objects') has no struct/record-defining pseudo-op -- its data/memory constructs (ERASABLE/FIXED MEMORY, EQUALS, 2DEC/2OCT, CADR/ECADR) are already fully covered by globals/memory_alloc/pointers. Contrast with the generic `assembly` entry (assembly.py:105-108), which DOES map class_start to struc/STRUCT/.struct macros -- proof the engine already detects struct pseudo-ops where they exist. AGC's narrower, real historical ISA genuinely has no equivalent directive; this is not an oversight relative to its sibling, it's a real capability gap between two different real assemblers.

GNU M4 is a pure text-substitution macro processor; neither M4 nor Autoconf (the corpus's real-world use case) has any record/object/type-declaration concept. func_start already covers macro definition (m4_define/AC_DEFUN); reviewing the full rules dict (m4.py) finds no other m4/autoconf idiom resembling a compound-type or entity boundary. Unlike yacc or fortran, there is no sibling 'macro processor with a type system' in the registry to suggest this is an engine gap rather than the language's actual shape.

GNU Make's model is variables plus file/phony targets; it has no entity or type-declaration concept. The one candidate construct, `define ... endef` (a named multi-line template), is already correctly wired to `macros` (makefile.py:216) rather than an object/entity boundary -- it defines a reusable text template, not a typed record, and double-wiring it to class_start would misrepresent it as an OOP-like boundary it isn't. No record/struct idiom exists anywhere in real Makefile usage.

Comment at shell.py:119-121: 'Shell is strictly procedural.' The one candidate construct, associative arrays (`declare -A`), is a data-structure instance, not a type/entity declaration, and isn't wired anywhere (pointers/immutability_locks/encapsulation cover declare -n/-r but not -A). Unlike tcl, which has real, idiomatic OOP frameworks (TclOO/Snit/Itcl, wired at tcl.py:70-72) precisely because tcl programmers commonly use them, there is no comparably common bash-native class convention in real-world scripts to anchor a rule to.

CSS is purely declarative with no embedded imperative/scripting payload, unlike the other languages that wire these three signals only against such payload: html's cleanup/telemetry fire on inline JS (removeEventListener/clearInterval, <script src=analytics>/sendBeacon); dockerfile's fire on shell build steps (apt-get clean, LOG_LEVEL); yaml's telemetry fires on GH Actions workflow commands (::debug/::warning/::error). CSS never carries any of that. cleanup: no destructor/teardown lifecycle exists -- rules are declaratively re-evaluated per paint; the closest analog (unset/initial/revert/revert-layer) is already claimed by panics_and_aborts, so a cleanup rule over the same tokens would double-count; clear:both is a layout primitive, not resource teardown. state_mutation: custom-property declarations and cascade overrides are declaration/specificity resolution, not temporal reassignment (no 'was A, now B' model) -- mirrors html's identical state_mutation=None/identical stated reasoning; css and html are the two purely-declarative languages in the taxonomy that null this signal while dockerfile/yaml (imperative-payload-bearing) wire it. telemetry: no logging/analytics primitive; scroll-driven-animation constructs are already captured by events/listeners. Corpus-confirmed: data/css/{b,c}.css's probe-state/probe-telemetry/probe-cleanup keyframes are empty placeholders -- bucket-3 test (could the shell plant something real?) fails for all three; nothing exists to author.

Embedded C action blocks are NOT routed through a separate C rule set: detector.py's Mode_A_Labels (~L2392, yacc has no entry in _lens_config.py's HANDSHAKE_REGISTRY) applies yacc's own rules over the whole rule body including its {..} actions, so a stray assert() in an action already lands under yacc's safety rule rather than going unmeasured. The corpus's function construct takes no parameter list in these languages, so `args` and `avg_func_args` read low by morphology, not by an authoring gap. Shared criterion, applied per language against the live registry (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the construct the corpus counts as a function (the language's `func_start` rule) declares no parameters, and the `args` rule matches some *other* construct entirely, so SPEC's "each probe taking exactly one argument where the language expresses arguments" has nothing to attach to. Corpus-wide `args` totals against the 13 median: css 3, html 3, dockerfile 4, yacc 2, makefile 1, sqlite 1, cobol 1, yaml 0; `avg_func_args` is 0 or near-0 in all eight for the same reason (the hits that do exist are not inside probe bodies). Per language, with the plant-anyway option priced by running the candidate through the live compiled rules (finditer, same screening method as A.1): (css) probes are at-rules and an at-rule takes a condition, not a parameter list; the args rule matches CSS functional notation (calc|clamp|min|max|var|env|url|rgb...) inside declarations, and all 3 hits are the `url("a.css")` of the @import chain in main/a/b (c is the leaf) — i.e. args here is a byproduct of the planted `import`, the third arm of css-import-url-io-triple-overlap. `width: calc(1px + 1px)` would raise it to 13 at zero overlap cost and is DECLINED: a value expression in a declaration body is not the at-rule's parameter. (html) probes are `<script>`/`<style>` tags (themselves unreachable end-to-end, gitgalaxy#2549) and the args rule matches ATTRIBUTES (data-*, aria-*, name, value, for, ...); the 3 hits are a.html's two `data-testid` and main.html's `name="author"` ownership meta — byproducts of other plants. `<input name= value=>` also fires `api` (planted and scored); a bare `data-probe=` is clean apart from unscored structural_boundaries, and is DECLINED on the same ground: an attribute is not an argument to a callable. (yacc) probes are grammar rules and `$$`/`$n` semantic-value references are the nearest thing yacc has to a parameter surface, so this one is rejected on OVERLAP COST rather than absence: `probe_x: TOKEN { $$ = $1; }` scores args 2 AND state_mutation 1 (b.y's existing state 2 is exactly that assignment plus a counter++), so actions in the 12 productions would add 12 to a planted, scored column to move an unplanted one — the same trade cobol rejected. (yaml) probes are `run:` steps and the args rule matches a `with:` block, which in GitHub Actions binds to a `uses:` step and never to `run:` — unreachable from the corpus's function shape. Planting it costs a `uses:` line, which fires `import` AND `_dependency_capture`: fake edges in the planted main->a->b->c DAG (import = 3 corpus-wide) that the graph layer cross-checks. REVERSED FOR `args` 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2753, engine PR #2759; corpus keyword-rosetta#59): the reasoning above is correct about `with:` and was written before anyone checked the OTHER half of yaml's parameter surface. `with:` supplies arguments to an action; what a workflow DECLARES is `inputs:` (`on: workflow_dispatch:`/`workflow_call:`, or action.yml's top-level `inputs:`), which the rule never matched, and the old regex counted a block as ONE argument rather than one per key (a composite action declaring 24 inputs read 0). #2753 rewrote the rule to match every indented mapping key behind a `yaml_parameter_block` scope filter that keeps the keys whose immediate parent is a valueless `with:`/`inputs:`/`args:` header. An `inputs:` block needs no `uses:` line, so the DAG objection above -- the actual reason this was declined -- does not reach it. The corpus now declares one input per function definition per file (main 4, a/b/c 3 = 13 = the median), and yaml's `args` cell is green. yaml stays in this entry for `avg_func_args` ALONE, which remains 0.0 by morphology: the corpus's function unit is a `run:` step, which has no parameter surface -- the workflow does, and a workflow-level declaration is not inside any step's body. (makefile) probes are targets (extraction fixed by gitgalaxy#2648) and targets take no parameters; make's parameter surface is `define`/`$(call f,...)`/`$(1)`, and `define` matches the registry's `macros` rule, NOT `func_start` — converting probes to macros would delete 12 planted func_start occurrences — while `$(call ...)` additionally fires `reflection_metaprogramming`, a scored input to risk_cognitive_load. main.mk's single hit is its one `$(call probe_branch)` dispatch. (dockerfile) probes are RUN/CMD/HEALTHCHECK instructions, which take no parameters; `ARG` is a file-scoped build variable and the corpus already plants one per file (FLAG/ENVKIT/SHAPE/PLAN = 4). Nine more ARG lines are overlap-free (finditer: args only, no `globals` — unlike ENV, which is dual globals+state) and DECLINED: no instruction would consume them, so args would be measuring how many ARG lines someone typed. (sqlite) probes are CREATE INDEX statements (the #2513 tri-comparison precedent) and an index takes no parameters; args matches bind placeholders (?1, :name), `VALUES (...)` row constructors and CTE parameter lists, all of which live in DML — and every DML verb that can carry one (SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|REPLACE) is also an `io` keyword in sqlite's own rule, so each args plant costs +1 io, against a language whose io is already the batch's largest residual (#2669 B.4). main.sql's one hit is its `VALUES (1)`. (cobol) full verdict in cobol-args-clause-match-morphology (paragraphs declare no parameters; the only argument surface is the program-level PROCEDURE DIVISION USING; every per-probe alternative is also an `api` keyword); listed here so the shape is one entry and so `avg_func_args` is covered, which that entry's args-only signal did not reach. NOT in this entry, deliberately: agc_assembly. Its args rule matches register-target operands (\b(CA|CS|TS|AD|SU|...)[ \t]+(A|Q|L|Z)\b) and the AGC calling convention really does pass an argument in the accumulator, so it HAS a parameter surface; #2669 A.3 planted `CA A` at each probe entry and took args 2 -> 13, avg_func_args 0.167 -> 1.0 (the median). REVERSED FOR cobol 2026-09-07 (gitgalaxy#2804 shape (a); corpus keyword-rosetta#97): cobol is REMOVED from languages_seen for both tokens, and is the third entry in this list to leave after agc_assembly and yaml's `args` half. Appending ` USING ARGV-BLOCK` to those nine lines is args +9 at zero marginal collateral (screened end-to-end: no other column moves in any file), taking corpus `args` 1 -> 10 against the 13 median, in band. `avg_func_args` stays 0.0 but NOT for the reason this entry gives -- there is now a parameter surface and the engine's own function record sees it (hit_vector.args = 1 per paragraph); what reads 0 is the per-function args field, computed off a Mode A window that for cobol never extends past the label's own line, leaving the ENTRY statement one line outside it. That is a separate, live cause with its own entry (cobol-entry-args-outside-mode-a-window, gitgalaxy#2863), so cobol leaves this entry entirely rather than staying on for avg_func_args the way yaml does -- yaml's `run:` step genuinely has no parameter surface, and keeping cobol here on a premise that is now false is exactly the excuse-a-cell-nobody-looked-at failure this file's _doc forbids. css BECOMES A STATED ABSENCE 2026-09-08 (gitgalaxy#2893; engine PR pending): the verdict's premise above is unchanged and is now recorded in the ENGINE instead of only here. The 6 retired hits were byproducts of other plants (3 @import url() + 3 probe-io url() steps), and `calc()` stays declined -- now declined by the engine, not by this entry. css STAYS in languages_seen for BOTH tokens, deliberately: `args` so the absence reads 'ledgered' rather than 'unreviewed' (docs/na_baseline.json is empty, so a single unreviewed absence fails na_check --ci), and `avg_func_args` because NOTHING ELSE WOULD COVER IT -- unmeasurable_risk_cells() spans risk_* columns only, explain_out_of_band()'s PER_FUNCTION_METRICS path fires only when functions_found is 0 (css reads 14), and the `derived` fallback reads `args` out of `oob`, which an n/a cell has left. apex's import rule is compiled with re.IGNORECASE, which neutralises the [A-Z] guard in its second alternative (\b[a-zA-Z_]\w*\.[A-Z]\w*\b), so the alternative degrades from "lowercase receiver, capitalised member" — a type reference — to "any word.word", and every qualified method call counts as an import. Micro-repro against the live registry (engine 3ac91822): 'foo.bar', 'conn.clear' and 'Logger.info' all match; recompiling the identical pattern WITHOUT re.IGNORECASE returns nothing for all three, which isolates the flag as the entire cause. 'System.debug' and 'Database.query' are correctly excluded by the namespace lookahead. Swept every language: apex is the only rule combining re.IGNORECASE with an [A-Z] guard. Corpus effect: import 6 against a planted intent and a cross-language median of 3 — main.cls Type.forName, a.cls Type.forName, b.cls Type.forName + Logger.info + Log.error, c.cls conn.clear. The three Type.forName hits are the SPEC chain planted by gitgalaxy#2669 A.3; the other three are ordinary Apex method calls and are deliberately NOT deleted, because removing them would hide the defect rather than record it. Before A.3 apex had no chain and the count read 3 — the right number for the wrong reason, which is why the rule survived the earlier sweeps. Same family as gitgalaxy#2544 (swift's api rule counting the prose 'open'): a guard that does not guard. Filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2671 with the fix shape (scope the guard with (?-i:[A-Z]) or split the alternation, keeping IGNORECASE for the Type.forName arm since Apex is case-insensitive); collected by #2669 B.1/B.3. apex re-blesses to import 3 once it lands. RESOLVED 2026-09-02: Fixed by gitgalaxy#2671: the [A-Z] guard is restored with a scoped (?-i:[A-Z]\w*) override, so re.IGNORECASE no longer degrades the type-reference alternative to `any word.word`. apex import reblessed 6 -> 3.

control_flow_ratio = branch / (branch + structural_boundaries) (gitgalaxy detector.py:1288). The corpus pins the numerator -- branch is 3-4 in every language by design -- and never plants, gates or reports the denominator, so the whole cross-language spread is structural_boundaries, measured 0-45. It cannot be equalised by planting, because it is not a structural count: it is a per-language KEYWORD VOCABULARY tally, and the vocabularies differ in kind. ada matches six structural words (procedure|function|package|begin|end|return); python matches sixteen; solidity matches those plus every type name (uint\d*, int\d*, bytes, address, mapping); assembly matches every instruction mnemonic (mov, lea, push, pop, add, sub, ldr, str). Measured on the a.* files, where planted intent is identical: solidity 10 hits of which SIX are the type name 'uint', python 9 (def x3, return x3, from, import, assert), ada 9 (procedure x3, begin x3, end x3). Every typed declaration in solidity scores a hit its python equivalent cannot. VERDICT: the metric is not broken and no engine change is wanted -- gitgalaxy compares control_flow_ratio between files WITHIN one repository (security_auditor.py reads it that way), where the vocabulary is held constant and the ratio means what it claims. Only the cross-language comparison this corpus performs is meaningless, so the cells are explained, not fixed. Recorded in gitgalaxy#2689 (Batch D.1) bucket B, which originally proposed planting the denominator -- that recommendation was withdrawn once the rule was read. 2026-09-04 (gitgalaxy#2729 corpus wave): javascript and typescript joined, and they are the cleanest demonstration the entry has. Their api plant is `export function`, and `export` is in their structural_boundaries vocabulary -- so the denominator grew by exactly 3 per file while the numerator stayed pinned at the planted branch count, and control_flow_ratio fell out of band with not one line of control flow changed. A metric that moves when a visibility keyword is added is measuring vocabulary, which is what this entry says. NARROWED (gitgalaxy#2770 / gitgalaxy#2789, 2026-09-06): this entry's reading of the SPREAD stands -- structural_boundaries is a vocabulary tally and the cross-language cells stay explained -- but two of its claims did not survive being checked against the code. (1) "No engine change is wanted" was scoped to control_flow_ratio itself and silently covered its derived consumer: dependency_density divided by max(int(coding_loc * control_flow_ratio), 1), so a GATED metric was reading this ungoverned denominator. gitgalaxy#2789 removed that -- dependency_density is now import_count / max(coding_loc, EVIDENCE_MASS_FLOOR), the #2655 doctrine every other per-file density already used -- and the column's cross-language consistency went 82.6% -> 93.5% here, where the old 82.6% was itself an artifact of the denominator collapsing to the constant 1. dependency_density is therefore no longer downstream of this entry. (2) The "gitgalaxy compares control_flow_ratio between files WITHIN one repository, where the vocabulary is held constant" defense has two holes, neither of which this entry had tested. It is a WITHIN-language defect that control_flow_ratio is 0 for any file with no branches at all. Measured over all 46 languages' 184 program shells: 133 of them (72%) record control_flow_ratio == 0, and in 39 of the 46 languages exactly three of the four shells do -- only main.* carries the planted branches, so a/b/c are branchless by the corpus's own design (one language has all four at zero; six have fewer than three). Any consumer multiplying by control_flow_ratio (dependency_density did; security_auditor.py's log_logic_loc still does) therefore sees a discontinuity when a single `if` is added, with the vocabulary held perfectly constant -- measured at 21x on yaml (denominator 1 -> 21) and 6x on python. And the within-repository premise itself only holds for a monolingual repo: security_auditor._build_feature_frame one-hot encodes language but applies no per-language normalisation and no groupby, so in a polyglot repository the vocabularies are NOT held constant in the very consumer this entry cites. The entry keeps still_reproduces true for control_flow_ratio's own cells; gitgalaxy#2770 shapes (a)/(b) remain the open question, and under shape (b) -- branch over coding_loc -- the metric becomes plantable and this entry retires rather than narrows.

entries.verdict: These five languages report functions_found = 16 against 13 planted. The three extra are not functions: the slicer synthesizes a __global_context__ bucket per file to hold top-level statements, and it is counted in the function population. Measured directly from the scan DB -- matlab and lua each carry exactly three __global_context__ rows in function_data alongside the 13 real probes, while python carries none. Every per-function descriptor therefore divides by 16 over a population containing three non-functions, diluting each by roughly 3/16, and cog_raw and structural_mass inherit it downstream. Same family as gitgalaxy#2547, which taught the orphan/duplicate checks to skip synthetic names via _is_synthetic_satellite_name; the per-function denominators were never given the same treatment. Filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2691 with that fix shape. Baking the current behaviour in per GATING.md rule 3 (the corpus measures what the engine does, not what it should); when #2691 lands, functions_found returns to the planted 13 and these manifests re-baseline in the same PR that flips still_reproduces. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2691, merged in gitgalaxy#2693): the engine now excludes its synthetic top-level buckets from the function population, via a `_UNCOUNTABLE_SLICE_NAMES` set narrower than the orphan check's own synthetic-name test. Verified by a fresh full-precision scan against the merged engine, not by hand: functions_found is 13 -- the planted value -- for all five languages (livecode, lua, matlab, ruby, shell), matching python. The buckets still exist and their signals are still counted at file level; only the population changed. Worth recording for whoever touches this next: the first version of the fix reused the broad orphan-check helper, which also covers "Main", and that removed go's real `func main()` from the count -- caught by tree-sitter accuracy at found_functions 897 -> 896.

These are the shape cells that survive every other explanation, and they are the interesting ones: mainstream procedural languages whose every INPUT is in band -- branch, args and LOC all green -- yet whose composite is not. The cause is the formula's deliberate non-linearity (signal_processor.py ~L800): sum_function_impacts = ((branch + 1) * sqrt(args + 1) + 0.05 * min(loc, (branch + args + 1) * 10)) * 10. A product and a clamp amplify input differences too small to flag on their own, which is precisely what makes cog_raw a cognitive-load proxy rather than a count -- a linear metric would just restate its inputs. VERDICT (gitgalaxy#2689 bucket E): affirmed as intended engine semantics, not bias, so no engine change and no re-banding. Widening the band for composites was considered and rejected: it would mask real regressions later, and the amplification is the signal. Also recorded there, so it is not re-proposed: the hypothesis that the median mixes procedural and config/DSL populations was TESTED AND REJECTED -- recomputing each metric's median over procedural languages only moves the out-of-band count by 0-1 cells (cog_raw 14 -> 14, avg_func_complexity 5 -> 5, func_internal_density 5 -> 6). SCOPE EXTENSION (2026-09-03, after gitgalaxy#2691 landed): lua's structural_mass joins this entry. It was previously attributed to the synthetic-bucket shape, and when that entry retired the cell resurfaced -- correctly, because the dilution was never the whole story for lua. Re-measured against the fixed engine: functions_found is now the planted 13 and every input is in band (branch +0%, args +0%, total_loc -5%, coding_loc -5%, state_mutation +0%), yet structural_mass sits at +41%. That is this entry's mechanism exactly. matlab's cog_raw and structural_mass resurfaced at the same moment and are NOT added here: matlab's state_mutation is +1150% (gitgalaxy#2654's return-convention shape), so its composites are attributed to that input deviation instead -- which the E.1 derivation table now does automatically, once it was corrected to include the inputs `_calc_cog_load` and `file_mass` actually read. RETIRED 2026-09-06 (Phase 0 decay check, keyword-rosetta#75's rule made standing by #77): gitgalaxy#2689 closed as design and E.1's derivation edges now attribute every composite to its out-of-band input automatically, so no cell rests on this entry (the decay check finds its 26-cell cross-product entirely in band or derived). Verifying scan: engine main 185061d1, full-precision regen 2026-09-06 (the run behind keyword-rosetta#80; CI bias-history regenerates on merge).

ada measures avg_func_args 3.0 against a corpus median of 1.0 (+200%) while planting exactly one parameter per probe function, like every other language. Cause traced to detector.py ~L6169: when a captured signature contains no comma the counter falls back to len(args_str.split()), a whitespace split written for Lisp/Scheme/Shell space-separated arguments. Ada's 'procedure Probe_Globals (Env : Integer)' captures 'Env : Integer', which splits into ['Env', ':', 'Integer'] -- one parameter counted as three. Confirmed per function in the scan DB: all 13 ada probes report args=3 where python's identical probes report 1. Ada is the ONLY language above the median here; the 0.825 cluster is the synthetic-bucket dilution (synthetic-global-context-bucket-counts-as-a-function) and the low outliers are args-no-parameter-surface-morphology. Multi-parameter ada is worse, not better, since Ada separates parameters with semicolons: 'X : Integer; Y : Integer' splits into six. Filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2692 with the fix shape; baking current behaviour in per GATING.md rule 3 until it lands. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2692, merged in gitgalaxy#2693): the comma-free argument fallback now splits on `;` first and treats a colon adjacent to whitespace as a type annotation, so a single typed parameter counts as one. Verified by fresh scan: ada avg_func_args is 1.0, exactly the corpus median and the planted value. The whitespace requirement is what preserves Lisp identifiers carrying a bare colon (`foo:bar`) as the separate arguments they are.

The residual shape cells after gitgalaxy#2689's other four mechanisms are accounted for, and they are all the same thing seen from two directions: identical planted intent occupies a different number of lines per language, and every one of these metrics is normalised by function body length. Measured against a corpus median avg_func_loc of 5.125: tcl 1.0 (-80%, a proc body the slicer captures as a single line) and cobol 3.19 (-38%) sit below, so their per-line densities and complexity spreads compress; haskell 0.094, jcl 0.083 and scheme 0.058 func_internal_density sit ABOVE a 0.034 median (+175%/+144%/+69%) for the mirror-image reason -- their function bodies are the shortest in the corpus (haskell 8.5 coding_loc, jcl 6.0) so the same planted signals concentrate into fewer lines. css is the degenerate case of the same rule: its 13 'functions' are selectors, which carry no branching at all, so max_func_complexity 0.25 vs 0.75 and func_complexity_gini 0.062 vs 0.188 are measuring the absence of a construct rather than a deviation in one. VERDICT: intended morphology, no engine change -- a language cannot be made to express the same logic in the same number of lines, which is the entire premise these metrics normalise against. Distinct from the ada, synthetic-bucket and composite-non-linearity entries, each of which has a mechanical cause; this one is the irreducible remainder.

detector.py L1383 is the whole definition of orphaned_logic: `elif len(func_name) > 3 and token_counts[func_name] <= 1` -- a function is an orphan when its identifier appears once in the file. token_counts is over the entire code stream INCLUDING the definition's own tokens, so the count is a property of the language's syntax, not of whether anything calls the function. There is no call graph behind this metric. Measured over the corpus (galaxyscope --db-only --debug, 46 languages, engine 4c283edf); baseline is 2.50 orphans/file (13 probe functions, 3 called from main). Five shapes, all of them here: (1) NAME REPEATED BY SYNTAX -> 0.00: ada closes with `end Probe_Globals;`, haskell writes `probeGlobals :: Int -> Int` above the equation, livecode ends the handler by name, so the token count is 2 before anything calls it. (2) SLICE NAME SYNTHETIC OR SHORT -> 0.00: yaml's 13 slices are all named `run` (3 chars, fails the len > 3 test); sqlite's are `Declarative_Block`/`CREATE_Statement`, excluded by _is_synthetic_satellite_name. (3) NO FUNCTIONS -> 0.00: html and markdown extract none, so the count has no value (D.2's undefined family, one metric further on). (4) NAME NEVER RECURS -> 3.25, i.e. every function orphaned: cobol paragraphs, m4 macros, scheme defines, make targets, abap forms, jcl steps and objective-c methods are written once and invoked by other means. (5) css 1.00: its three @keyframes slices share the name `keyframes`, which suppresses them, leaving only main.css's media/supports/container. Identical planted intent in every language, so the whole spread is measurement. entries.verdict: m4 args 18 vs a median of 13 (SPEC: 13 function definitions, one argument each). m4 macros have no parameter list -- `define(probe_globals, ...)` names no parameters and `$1` inside the body IS the parameter, so the rule counts one arg per USE, not per declaration: a.m4 5, b.m4 4, c.m4 3, main.m4 6 against 3/3/3/4 definitions. Every other language declares its one argument once in a signature and uses it however often it likes. The plant is correct (each macro takes exactly one argument); the count is the language's syntax, and equalising it would mean writing macros that never reference their own argument.

csharp globals 3 vs a median of 2. a.cs carries the two planted globals (`ConfigurationManager`, `AsyncLocal`); the third is in main.cs, where the planted high_risk_execution call `Environment.Exit(payload)` also matches the globals rule's `Environment.` prefix -- one token, two rules, both correct in isolation. The cell is n/a here rather than a -100% outlier because there is no population to compare (the structure-count n/a mechanism, gitgalaxy#2795). Golden master re-blessed: 17 differences, every one a sqlite cognitive-load term re-solving off a func_complexity_gini that no longer describes statement buckets. DOCKERFILE'S HALF STANDS, and #2792 re-tested it rather than inheriting the earlier deferral. dockerfile's func_start is a closed keyword alternation (RUN|CMD|ENTRYPOINT|HEALTHCHECK), and excluding those names from the population also drops their rows from `function_data` -- the record the engine's own tree_sitter_accuracy_audit compares against the grammar. The same reading covers css 14 (+8%, green), yaml 13 (on the median) and html 0 (its own entry). The count still scales with instruction volume rather than with the planted program -- that is the inherency this entry records, and no engine change can move it. Related but distinct: gitgalaxy#2728 is about those same buckets reaching the duplicate and orphan checks as if they were real identifiers, which IS a defect and is fixed.

betweenness_score javascript and python 0.05 against a median of 0.0833335, with identical dependency_links (3) and popularity (0.75) -- so the DAG's edges are right and its SIZE is not. These are the only two language folders carrying an ecosystem manifest beside the four probe files: `package.json` and `pyproject.toml`. Betweenness is normalised by node count (network_risk_sensor.py's nx.betweenness_centrality), so a fifth scanned artifact lowers every centrality in the folder -- pagerank 0.2029 vs 0.2240 and closeness 0.1917 vs 0.2396 move with it. The manifests are deliberate (they are what exercises dependency extraction and the SBOM for those two ecosystems); the alternative is to exclude non-probe artifacts from the graph, which would change what the corpus measures about real repositories.

Haskell declares its whole public surface once, in the module header (`module A (probeGlobals, probeTest, probeSafety) where`), not per definition -- there is no per-function visibility keyword in the language. The api rule matches that header, so the corpus records api 1 per file against a per-function median of 3, and the count is a property of the idiom, not of how much surface the file exposes: the same header exports three probes. Planted 2026-09-04 under gitgalaxy#2729 (before it, every language's api read the converted orphan count and this difference was invisible). The header line also matches haskell's encapsulation rule (+1 per file), pinned in the manifest. Languages whose export idiom happens to be repeatable per function (scheme `(export x)`, tcl `namespace export x`, powershell `Export-ModuleMember -Function x`) plant 3 and are not in this shape.

These languages have no per-function visibility construct at all, so their api rule matches a FILE-level declaration and the corpus plants one per file: css `@property --probe-api-<file>` (custom-property registration; `:root` was rejected -- it also matches css's globals rule, a planted count), html `<div id=...>` (main reads 2: its `name="author"` ownership meta is also an api match), dockerfile `EXPOSE <port>` (also listeners + ipc_rpc_bridges, both ungated), yaml an `on:` trigger block, yacc `%define api.pure full`, agc_assembly one central-register `EQUALS` erasable assignment (also memory_alloc; c.agc reads 0 because spatial_correlation's leak/UAF dampener fires within 800 chars of its cleanup plants), cobol `LINKAGE SECTION.` in main. So api 1 per file against a per-function median of 3 is the idiom, not less surface. cobol's copybooks are the exception that proves it: `ENTRY 'PROBE-X'` IS per paragraph, so a/b/c plant 3 and only main reads 1. Planted 2026-09-04 under gitgalaxy#2729; before it every one of these read its converted orphan count instead of its rule. jcl joined 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2748): `//ROSPROC PROC` ... `// PEND` in main.jcl -- the procedure declaration the 13 EXEC ROSPROC steps invoke -- reads api 1 in main and 0 in a/b/c, the file-level shape (STEP2 moved inside the proc body, so func_start stays 4).

Seven languages define an api rule and still record 0 after the gitgalaxy#2729 wave, for two distinct reasons, both measured in the real pipeline before the plant was rejected. (1) The rule cannot see the language's own way of making a function public: abap's FORM subroutines are public by default and the rule wants PUBLIC SECTION / REMOTE FUNCTION / EXPOSED / DEFINE VIEW, all of which need a CLASS (class_start must stay 0), RFC metadata or a CDS definition; matlab function files have no visibility syntax and the rule counts only classdef `methods` blocks; dart's public top-level functions are invisible to a rule that counts class/mixin/enum/extension/typedef declarations; objective-c's public method declaration in an @interface is invisible to a rule that counts FOUNDATION_EXPORT/OBJC_EXPORT/extern/@property; ada's rule matches a package SPEC (`package X is`) and the corpus ships .adb bodies, where a spec would be a separate compilation unit. dart and objective-c CAN be made to fire with a manufactured declaration (a typedef per probe, a property per probe) and both were measured doing so cleanly, but planting a declaration nobody would write to make the number move is exactly the measurement the corpus exists to avoid, so both stay 0 and the gap is the finding. (2) The only construct the rule accepts moves a PLANTED count: perl's `@EXPORT_OK = qw(...)` adds state_mutation +1 per file (measured: a 0->1, b 3->4, c 1->2), `push @EXPORT_OK` is state_mutation by definition, `use Exporter|parent|base` is an import hit and `our` a globals hit; sqlite's `CREATE [TEMP] VIEW` is a func_start hit in every spelling the rule accepts (and its SELECT body an io hit), `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` a class_start hit. A corpus that moves a planted count to light up a signal is measuring itself. Both halves are the same finding as the one gitgalaxy#2729 was filed for -- the api rules disagree about what a public surface is -- and the rule-too-narrow half is filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2730, which asks for a stated contract for the api rule rather than seven separate regex fixes. Resolves per language as #2730 lands, paired with the plant that the widened rule can see (AGENTS.md rule 8). RESOLVED IN PART 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2730, shipped as #2743): the rule was given a stated contract -- *a declaration that makes a named function or type visible outside this file* (gitgalaxy docs/api_rule_contract.md) -- and audited against it in all 46 languages. Five of the seven are fixed at the rule, with no plant invented to chase them: abap counts a `FORM` subroutine (public by default, line-anchored so `CALL FUNCTION` cannot match), ada a column-0 library-level subprogram, dart a top-level function without a leading underscore, matlab a column-0 `function` (its file-level fallback -- a function file has no visibility syntax at all), perl a `sub` (package-public, which also sidesteps the state_mutation/import collision that made every other perl form unusable). All five now read api 3 per file, 4 in main. Two remain, for different reasons. objective-c's `@interface` method declaration IS now visible to the rule -- the engine half is done -- but the corpus still reads 0, because planting an `@interface` would create a class and SPEC.md rule 2 pins class_start at 0 as a false-positive tripwire in every language; that is a corpus constraint, not a rule gap, and it is why this entry stays open for objective-c rather than resolving with the other five. sqlite is unchanged: every spelling its rule accepts (`CREATE [TEMP] VIEW`, `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE`) is a func_start or class_start hit, so there is still no form that does not move a planted count.
