entries.verdict: In these four the api plant NAMES the probe functions -- `global probe_x` (NASM), `Export-ModuleMember -Function probe_x`, `module_function :probe_x`, `namespace export probe_x` -- and that second occurrence of the name makes the function stop reading as an orphan: detector.py ~L1383 defines an orphan as `token_counts[func_name] <= 1` over the whole code stream, with no call graph (gitgalaxy#2727). orphaned_logic therefore reads 0, the Contextual Baseline Fix has nothing to convert, and api_orphan_credit drops 3 -> 0 in a/b/c while `api` goes 0 -> 3. The import chain still resolves (import counts unchanged), so the credit's loss is not evidence of a DAG regression -- but the credit is the gate's only assertion that the chain resolved (GATING.md 'What `api` asserts'), so these four lose that assertion and rely on the other 40 for it. Name-free alternatives exist for some (`Export-ModuleMember -Function *`, a bare `module_function`, tcl `package provide`) and were rejected: they export the entry function too, or drop the count to 1, which is worse measurement to protect a side assertion. makefile `.PHONY: probe_x` and m4 `m4_provide([probe_x])` were rejected for this exact reason during the wave -- both zeroed the credit, and `export VAR` / `AC_SUBST` plant the same api count without naming a function, so those two languages keep their credit. Resolves when gitgalaxy#2727 makes the orphan census count occurrences outside the function's own span: a mention in an export statement is outside the span, so it will still clear the flag -- the honest fix is a real call graph, which #2727 records as the open design question. SIGNAL SCOPE: the same fact is visible in the bias report as `raw_state_slop_orphans` (3.25 -> 0 per file in these four against a corpus median of 2.50), which is the column the report measures; `api_orphan_credit` is the manifest key for it. Both are named so the gate and the report join on the same finding. shell JOINS this shape 2026-09-05. gitgalaxy#2730 made `export -f name` matchable (the old rule demanded a bare identifier straight after `export`, so the `-f` form -- the only way a shell script publishes a FUNCTION rather than a variable -- could never match), and the plant moved from `export PROBE_GLOBALS=1` to `export -f probe_globals`. api stays 3 per file; the count was never the point. The old plant exported a VARIABLE whose name merely resembled the probe, so shell's api cell was green for the wrong reason -- exactly the class of measurement gitgalaxy#2729's wave exists to remove. The cost is this entry's cost: `export -f probe_globals` names the function, so under gitgalaxy#2727's name-recurrence census the probe stops reading as an orphan and api_orphan_credit drops 3 -> 0. That cost is no longer distinctive -- api-declared-orphans-are-not-new-surface takes 25 more languages to the same place in the same PR -- so the trade that this entry previously refused for makefile and m4 is now worth making for shell, where the alternative is measuring the wrong construct. RETIRED 2026-09-06 (Phase 0 decay check, keyword-rosetta#75's rule made standing by #77): gitgalaxy#2727 fixed by PR #2754 (references, not name repetitions), and the api_orphan_credit column it explained is no longer gated; the entry's 10-cell cross-product is entirely in band. entries.verdict: Markdown is prose: no execution model (concurrency, sync_locks), no visibility construct (encapsulation), no const/freeze concept (immutability_locks), no metaprogramming facility (reflection_metaprogramming). Fenced code blocks are literate content owned by the #691 lit_* comment-stream rules, not commented-out code, so dead_code has nothing distinct to measure. spec_exposure's generic bracket-tag pattern ([SPEC-n]/[spec .../[audit ...]) collides with markdown link syntax -- any link whose text begins spec/audit would FP -- so that absence is deliberate, not an oversight. Completes the prose-morphology family alongside the existing markdown structure/signal entries.

No async-execution construct exists in these languages, per-language: css -- declarative styling; animations/transitions are declarative timelines the renderer schedules, nothing code-visible is asynchronous execution. jcl -- steps within a job execute strictly sequentially by definition; parallelism lives in JES scheduling/config outside the language's own syntax. m4 -- strictly sequential single-threaded text expansion. solidity -- the EVM executes transactions atomically and single-threaded; no threads/async/futures (the reentrancy surface is already owned by sync_locks nonReentrant and reflection_metaprogramming delegatecall/call). yacc -- a grammar has no execution model of its own; considered %pure-parser / %define api.pure (declares the generated parser's reentrancy, i.e. the absence of shared state, rather than serializing access to it) and rejected.

No lock/serialization construct exists, per-language: css and html -- markup and styling have no shared mutable state to serialize (html's closest stability idioms readonly/disabled/inert are already owned by its immutability_locks rule). m4 -- sequential expansion, no shared state. yacc -- grammar layer, same reasoning as its concurrency absence. yaml -- the one mutex-shaped construct in yaml.py's target ecosystem, GitHub Actions concurrency: groups (with cancel-in-progress), is already owned by the concurrency rule (^concurrency:); a sync_locks rule would re-count the same token -- the cobol-api overlap-cost rejection precedent.

No visibility/privacy construct: jcl -- PROCs and symbolic parameters are parameterization, not privacy; nothing in JCL syntax hides one statement from another. yaml -- plain data; GH Actions secrets.* is access to a secret store and is already owned by the globals rule (${{ secrets. }}), not an encapsulation idiom.

immutability_locks: JCL has no const concept. Considered LABEL=(,,,IN) read-only open and PROTECT=YES -- dataset-protection attributes, rare in real decks, not language-level immutability; rejected. reflection_metaprogramming: symbolic substitution (SET &X= / &X. use-sites) is parameterization -- SET is already owned by state_mutation, and the analogous shell $VAR expansion is likewise not counted as reflection in shell.py. Strongest candidate INCLUDE MEMBER=&NAME (dynamic include) rejected: parameterized inclusion, owned by import.

The engine's own registry records the rationale in-code: m4.py annotates the None rule with 'M4 macros are mutable by design'. define/undefine freely rebind any macro at any time -- mutability is the language's core mechanism; no freeze/const construct exists to measure.

RESOLVED by gitgalaxy#2732 (PR #2736); corpus plants land in this repo's companion PR. Original finding stands: dead_code (jcl) and spec_exposure (jcl, yaml) were comment-stream rules absent where the stream exists -- for jcl the #2610 leftover (the comment stream was structurally empty until _strip_jcl_comments, and #2610 added debt/ownership without revisiting these two); evidence, 13 of the 443 licensed pool .jcl/.prc files carry //*-commented-out statements (16 occurrences), including whole JOB cards. CORRECTION to this entry's original reasoning, recorded because the filed issue inherited it: yaml's absence was called arbitrary on the grounds that 'flow-sequence brackets cannot FP because spec_exposure never sees the code stream'. That is false. detector.coding_analysis applies EVERY non-underscore rule to the code stream and comment_analysis then adds a second pass over the comments -- it supplements the code-stream pass rather than replacing it. Measured: the generic unanchored rule scores spec_exposure=1 on a comment-free workflow containing only `needs: [audit, lint]`. YAML is the one language where a bracket holding bare unquoted words is ordinary syntax rather than a tag, so the absence was less arbitrary than it looked. Both shipped rules are therefore anchored to their language's comment marker (^[ \t]*# for yaml, ^//\* for jcl), matching yaml's own dead_code and jcl's own ownership rule; a `\b` was also added after the tag alternation because the bare `spec` branch otherwise matches 'specified'/'species' (2 of 3 code-stream hits across 41,815 pool .yml/.yaml files). Scope note retained: yaml/dead_code is NOT covered by this entry -- yaml defines that rule, so its 0 is a pre-existing comparable measurement.

Real serialization morphology with a rule-design conflict: DISP=OLD/MOD request an exclusive system ENQ on a dataset (DISP=SHR shared) -- z/OS's native lock idiom, and the engine already maps sync_locks onto a language's own idiom (solidity nonReentrant). But DISP= is already a keyword in jcl's io rule, and #2610 explicitly rejected a cleanup rule on DISP=(...,DELETE/CATLG) for exactly that double-count; counterweight: the engine tolerates semantic overlaps where meanings differ (COND=((4,LT),EVEN) counts safety AND safety_bypasses; haskell finally counts cleanup+safety). Filed as a design question with a narrowed OLD/MOD-only shape. Either outcome -- rule added with a paired DISP=OLD plant, or declined per the cleanup precedent -- ends the unreviewed state; this entry flips to record the decision. RESOLVED 2026-09-05, and the paired plant DECLINED with the reasoning recorded here because keyword-rosetta#59 asked for the call either way. The design question is decided: gitgalaxy#2733 shipped as #2742, narrowing sync_locks to `DISP=OLD|MOD` only -- SHR is the shared default every job asks for and NEW allocates, so neither declares a serialization decision -- and accepting the residual `io` overlap deliberately, on the COND=/haskell-finally precedent. jcl's sync_locks is therefore a measured 0 now, not an n/a. AGENTS.md rule 8 asks for a paired plant when a new rule turns an honest n/a into a manufactured red cell. It did not here, and planting would CREATE the red cell rule 8 exists to prevent: `sync_locks` is in the report's ungated unplanted-input set, so jcl's 0 costs nothing, while the plant `//DD3 DD DSN=CORPUS.TMP,DISP=(OLD,DELETE)` was screened against the live rules and lands `sync_locks` 1 AND `io` 1 -- and jcl's io is 3 against a median of 3, so +1 takes it to 4 and out of band, a gated cell that would then need an entry of its own. One ungated 0 traded for one gated red cell is a bad trade. Revisit if gitgalaxy#2749 lands a `cleanup` rule on `DISP=(...,DELETE)`: the same DD line would then pay a cleanup plant too, and the io cost is worth re-pricing against two signals rather than one. PLANTED AFTER ALL 2026-09-05 (keyword-rosetta#60): the revisit condition this entry named fired the same day. gitgalaxy#2749's `cleanup` rule on normal-position `DISP=(...,DELETE)` shipped in gitgalaxy#2755, so the single DD line now pays a `cleanup` plant as well as a `sync_locks` one, and the `io` cost is re-priced against two signals instead of one -- which is the trade #59 said would be worth making. c.jcl carries `//DD3 DD DSN=&&TMP1,DISP=(OLD,DELETE)` (sync_locks 1, cleanup 1, io 1) alongside `//DD4 DD DSN=&&TMP2,DISP=(,DELETE),UNIT=SYSDA` (cleanup 1, io 1); the resulting `io` over-read is ledgered under probe-idiom-collides-with-measured-signal, where jcl already sits. sync_locks is a measured 1, not an n/a; the design question is closed.

entries.verdict: api_orphan_credit drops 3 -> 0 in a/b/c (makefile 4 -> 3 in c.mk) across 25 languages, and it is the intended consequence of gitgalaxy#2731 landing as gitgalaxy#2734. The credit is `arch_api - raw_arch_api`: what galaxyscope.py's Contextual Baseline Fix adds on top of the api rule's own count when an imported file has uncalled functions. It used to add ALL of them, so a function that is both declared public and uncalled counted twice -- data/go/a.go recorded function_count 3, raw_arch_api 3, raw_state_slop_orphans 3 and arch_api 6, three functions for six units of public surface (that measurement is what filed #2731). detector.py now reports `api_declared_orphans` -- how many of the file's orphans the api rule matched at their own declaration, tested by NAME, which is exact because an orphan's name occurs exactly once in the file by definition -- and the conversion credits only `orphans - api_declared_orphans`. In this corpus every probe function is declared public by its language's own idiom (the gitgalaxy#2729 wave planted exactly that) AND uncalled in its own file, so the overlap is total and the credit is correctly 0. The debt wipe is unchanged and unconditional, so orphaned_logic stays 0: the file is imported, and an already-public orphan is surface the rule counted already, not dead weight. COST, recorded rather than worked around: the credit was the gate's only assertion that the main->a->b->c import chain resolved (it is how gitgalaxy#2543 and #2540 were caught, see api-export-names-suppress-orphan-credit, which had already lost it for four languages). 26 of 46 languages now assert 0 for it. The chain is still asserted by every language's `import` count and by the 20 languages whose api rule does not reach every probe. abap, dart, matlab and perl join this shape only because gitgalaxy#2730 made their own visibility idiom visible to the api rule in the first place -- before it their api was 0 and the conversion had nothing to overlap with. ada does not appear here: its syntax repeats the subprogram name (`end Probe_Globals;`), so under gitgalaxy#2727's name-recurrence census its probes were never orphans and its credit was already 0. dockerfile and scheme JOIN 2026-09-05, by a different route and a different upstream fix: gitgalaxy#2754 (closing #2727/#2728) rewrote the orphan census itself, so these two stopped having orphans to convert rather than having them subtracted. dockerfile's `RUN`/`HEALTHCHECK` slices are igniter-keyword buckets, not identifiers, and no longer enter the orphan check at all (#2728); a.dockerfile's credit 1 -> 0. scheme's probes are hyphenated (`probe-globals`), and the old census tokenised with `\b\w+\b`, which cannot produce a token containing a hyphen -- every such name counted ZERO occurrences and satisfied `<= 1` unconditionally, so all three probes per file read as orphans however many times they were named. With the census matching the literal name they are correctly seen in their own `(export probe-globals)` line, and a/b/c's credit drops 3 -> 0. Same visible cell, same verdict, two different engine causes -- recorded here rather than split, because the corpus reading is identical and a reader chasing `api_orphan_credit == 0` needs both explanations in one place. RETIRED 2026-09-06 (Phase 0 decay check, keyword-rosetta#75's rule made standing by #77): fixed by gitgalaxy#2734 (#2731) and the manifests re-blessed (api_orphan_credit 3 -> 0 in a/b/c corpus-wide); the 27-manifest citations stay as the history of that re-bless, but the deviation itself no longer reproduces anywhere. Verifying scan: engine main 185061d1, full-precision regen 2026-09-06 (the run behind keyword-rosetta#80; CI bias-history regenerates on merge). CORRECTION 2026-09-06 (gitgalaxy#2823): the scheme half of the 2026-09-05 paragraph above records the right number for the wrong reason. It says scheme's probes are 'correctly seen in their own `(export probe-globals)` line' -- they are not, and never were. api_declared_orphans tokenises the api-matched line with `\b\w+\b`, the same tokenizer gitgalaxy#2754 removed from the census itself and left here, and it cannot produce a token holding a hyphen. What actually happened is that #2754 left the `(export probe-x)` line clearing the ORPHAN flag (an export is a declaration, not a reference), so scheme had no orphans to convert and the credit fell to 0 upstream of this mechanism entirely. #2823 fixes that, scheme's orphans come back, and the credit returns to 3 in a/b/c -- the double count this entry exists to describe, still live for every language whose names are not all-\w. Filed as gitgalaxy#2827 and tracked in its own entry (api-declared-orphans-blind-to-non-word-names); scheme's manifest is re-blessed to 3 meanwhile. dockerfile's half of that paragraph is unaffected and still correct.

entries.verdict: agc_assembly reads high_risk_execution 2 against a median 3 because it is the one language in the corpus that cannot carry SPEC §Decoys' string decoy. The +1 every other language shows on this row is the danger-only literal, not a probe: the SPEC plants 2 (agc's are CURTAINS and WHIMPER in main.agc's PROBERISK) and the decoy asserts the third. The AGC assembler has no character-literal type at all -- its data pseudo-ops are OCT, DEC, 2DEC, ERASE and =/EQUALS, every one numeric -- so there is no data position a danger token can occupy that is not an instruction position, and SPEC §Decoys' own 'Skip only if the language has no string literals' clause applies. A symbol name is not a way round it either: agc's danger rule is \b-anchored, so HALTFLAG EQUALS 1 matches nothing, and a bare HALT label would be a real instruction, not a literal. What agc DOES carry is the comment decoy, and it is the strongest one in the corpus -- main.agc's '# DECOY: THIS SUITE NEVER REACHES CURTAINS AND THE HALT WORD STAYS IN PROSE' is the only decoy line anywhere naming two danger keywords, and it contributes 0, which is the comment-stripping half of the same experiment. Both are now recorded in the manifest's decoys array. Verified 2026-09-06 against engine main: verify_language.py agc_assembly PASS, 80 assertions, high_risk_execution 2/0/0/0. This entry replaces string-literal-selective-shielding as the explanation for this cell -- agc_assembly was listed in that entry's languages_seen despite never having carried the literal it describes. 2026-09-08 gitgalaxy#2878: this entry is now the cell's only explanation on the report side too -- batch4-dual-keyword-overlaps dropped high_risk_execution from its signal union, so categorize_out_of_band no longer takes that entry's extraction category over this one's inherency. The contract (docs/high_risk_execution_rule_contract.md C2) states the decoy's +1 as the stream contract's fact, not this signal's.

gitgalaxy#2765 gave state_mutation a stated contract (docs/state_mutation_rule_contract.md): one hit is a statement that writes a new value into state that already exists -- a declaration is not a write (even `var`/`let mut`/`int x = 5`), a type or modifier naming mutable state is not a write, a read/bind/cast is not a write, and one statement is one hit with no token another rule owns. Before it, 46 languages carried three incompatible definitions (named verbs / mutable declarations / every `=`), which is why state_mutation (60%) and risk_state_flux (42%) were the corpus's two worst metrics. RESOLVED upstream by the #2765 engine PR (30 rule rewrites) and re-blessed here in the same change. Cells that moved because the RULE was wrong: haskell a.hs 2->0 (IORef type signatures), dockerfile a 2->0 (ENV is globals), c a 2->0 and b 3->2 (declarations), go b 5->2 (`:=` and `_ =`), objective-c b 3->2, perl b 3->2 and c 1->0 (`my` declarations, bare shift), m4 c 2->0 (popdef is cleanup), apex c 1->0 (.clear( is cleanup), matlab c 1->0 and b cleanup 2->0 (clear is cleanup). Cells that moved because the PLANT was authored to the old rule: cpp, java, javascript, kotlin, rust, scala, swift, typescript, zig, solidity (mutable declarations / casts, re-planted as real writes), sqlite (UPDATE...SET counted twice, ALTER TABLE added as the second statement), livecode/scheme/tcl (the decoy line was a third write, one plant removed), abap (the `=` statement joined the rule, APPEND dropped). probe_debt bodies in abap/fortran/matlab/powershell assigned into languages with no declaration syntax and carried a state_mutation into a file planted at 0; rewritten to declare or return instead. Verifying scan: all 46 languages pass against gitgalaxy fix/2765-state-mutation-contract; state_mutation reads 2 in every b file and 0 elsewhere (jcl b keeps its ledgered SET dual). Still narrower than the contract, by design for now: python/embedded_python/ruby never count a plain local re-assignment -- filed as gitgalaxy#2817, not a red cell (their plants are container writes).

The branch rule counts a keyword that is not a runtime decision, one per language, each documented in the manifest notes and each a corollary of the branch contract gitgalaxy#2822 asks for. Three shapes: (A) a HANDLER keyword dual with safety -- cpp `catch` in a.cpp, ruby `rescue` in a.rb (finditer-confirmed in both manifests); (B) the SYNTAX WORDS of one conditional -- swift's `guard` plus its own `else` clause in main.swift (4 = if + else + guard + guard-else), sqlite's single CASE expression counting CASE/WHEN/THEN/ELSE/END (5); (C) `goto` dual with high_risk_execution -- csharp main.cs (4 = if/else/switch + goto). Sibling per-language entries record the same shapes where a language was swept earlier: ada-end-if-branch-inflation (B), shell-test-brackets-in-branch (B), fortran-goto-dual-branch-highrisk (C), and the livecode/powershell/tcl/makefile duals inside batch4-dual-keyword-overlaps (A/B). 27 of 46 branch rules name catch/rescue/except/goto; the 38 languages reading 3 simply plant their safety construct with a token their branch rule does not match. Found 2026-09-06 when string-literal-selective-shielding's cross-product was narrowed: these five cells had been excused by an entry that could not explain them. Current behaviour baked in per GATING.md; retire with the engine fix. RETIRED 2026-09-06: fixed by gitgalaxy#2822's engine PR. (A) cpp catch and ruby rescue -- and every handler keyword corpus-wide -- left branch (safety's); (B) swift's guard-else no longer double-counts (else anchors on '}') and sqlite's CASE counts CASE + its WHEN/ELSE arms only (5->3); (C) csharp goto left branch (high_risk_execution owns it). All five cells re-blessed to plant.

a.ts reads safety 3 against a plant of 2: `unknown` twice (a parameter type and a local's type) plus `never`. typescript's safety rule lists `unknown|never|void` alongside try/catch/finally -- TYPE keywords counted as runtime guards. A type annotation is not a defensive construct any more than `IORef Int` is a write (state_mutation corollary 2) -- the same count-contract question as gitgalaxy#2822's branch shapes, from the safety side, and audited with it. It decides the overlap by tokenising each api-matched LINE with `\b\w+\b` and testing the orphan's name for membership, and that tokenizer cannot produce a token containing `-`, `:`, `.`, `!` or `?`. It is the same tokenizer family as gitgalaxy#2754, which fixed the census itself and left this consumer behind. cobol has carried it since #2734: `PROBE-GLOBALS` is never matched in the api line that declares its own paragraph, 3 per file in a/b/c. scheme JOINS 2026-09-06 with gitgalaxy#2823 -- until then its export line was wrongly clearing the orphan flag, so there were no orphans to double-count and the cell read 0 for an unrelated reason (see the correction on api-declared-orphans-are-not-new-surface). haskell is the control that proves the diagnosis: its probes are named in `module A (probeGlobals, probeTest, probeSafety) where`, all three tokens are plain \w, api_declared_orphans reads 3 and the credit correctly stays 0. makefile reads dead_code 7 where every other language in the corpus carrying the same comments reads 0. All 7 are prose: `# decoy:` x4 (the shell furniture one per file), `# HACK:` (the fragile_debt plant), `# TODO:` (planned_debt) and `# author:` (ownership). Cause: makefile's dead_code rule is the only comment-anchored one in the registry that is SHAPE-anchored rather than keyword-anchored -- its first alternative is `<identifier>[ \t]*::?`, which every `Label: text` prose comment satisfies, while shell, python and yaml all require a real keyword (`if|for|while|def|class|run:|uses:|...`).
